knn_amd_legacy_schedule.note: Rollback arm: AMD back to its old IDENTICAL kNN rows (query tile 256, no radix scratch shrink, no resident derived cache, generic-K selector without warp-bound guard, no bound-and-compact at k>=17, 4 register rows, scalar index loads). Default: AMD takes NVIDIA's rows. Kept per-vendor: hardware FTZ FMA (NVVM instruction, no AMD spelling) and the AMD smem tile d>=32 gate (measured AMD loss). NVIDIA build unchanged by this control.

knn_scratch_pool_off.note: Rollback arm: per-call allocation of queries, norms, dist_tile, radix pairs, outputs and pinned readback on every resident search. Default: exact-length views of the handle's high-water pool.

knn_widek_radix.note: On a 64-lane column (AMD CDNA) k>=17 column-tile selection by the radix selector (scratch shrink skipped there). NVIDIA build unaffected (32-lane). Same composite-key total order.

knn_amd_block_topk_all_k.note: AMD column only: block top-k serves k up to 64 (no distance matrix, no selector launch) where the smem tile runs (d>=32 on AMD). NVIDIA keeps 16.

knn_amd_exact_chain.note: AMD column only: the register tile (d<32 on AMD) admits proven tiles to the unflushed chain. Time on taxi-like narrow rows.
